10/27/2026
10/27/26 15:09 This dog has demonstrated a persistent, recurring pattern of fluctuating in-kennel stress and anxiety, ranging from moderate to significant, over an extended period of time. These behaviors are often a response to the overwhelming sights, sounds, and confinement, along with the lack of choice or control over their environment. Although this dog continues to show appropriate behavior outside of the kennel with positive interactions with staff and volunteers, without intervention, well-being will continue to decline. Immediate placement is needed with an experienced adopter or New Hope Partner who can provide time and space to decompress in a calm, supportive home. Placement needed by close of business 11/1/26. May be at risk of euthanasia 11/2/26 or sooner if warranted.

Dog exited kennel, lowered head, tense, sniffed a nearby bush for a moment, handler was able to adjust stopper while dog sniffed. Walked slightly behind handler to yard, handler attached extra leash. Dog wandered yard, still tail above spine level, avoiding eye contact with handlers. Assistant moved to opposite catch pen to close outer gate, dog paused and watched, assistant tossed treats, dog sniffed ground, ignored assistant. Dog wandered independently, gradually becoming less tense with still tail at spine level, looser musculature, but had deeply furrowed brow, tightly closed mouth, and ears upright throughout entire evaluation. Dog defecated, handler moved to get bag, dog watched for a moment, then resumed sniffing ground. Dog sniffed along fence line, briefly whining, sniffed behind the bench where handlers were sat, did not look up or attempt to approach handlers, walked away. Dog walked around kiddie pool, leash became stuck, dog flinched away when pool moved, recovered fairly quickly. Handler held out hand and softly called to dog as he passed by, dog whale eyed handler and whined. After a few more minutes of sniffing and urine marking, assistant began tossing treats to dog, dog attempted to catch, would sniff them out on ground. Assistant gradually tossed treats closer, dog followed, slightly low, wide stance. When assistant stopped throwing treats, dog was about 5-6 feet away, sniffed ground, then froze and hard stared at assistant with short, tight lip, and alarm barked, disengaged on his own, continued to sniff ground. Both handlers tossed a few treats away, handler walked to catch pen, dog entered, allowed handler to pick up leash, handler adjusted stopper as dog sniffed ground. sections.evaluation_comments:
10/27/2026
Updating color due to NHO status.
10/20/2026
Responding to loose dog call on radio* Dog was standing up alongside fence with eyes wide, ears alert, wary of ACT staff member placing leash while heavily panting, pawing towards leash to push away, allowed handler to slowly approach and place leash over head. Became erratic on leash, zig zag walking pattern, strong pull back to kennel, began thrashing/pulling on leash when approaching kennel, able to guide dog into kennel as dog thrashed with no issues, tense bodied while sitting in middle of kennel, would not come forward as handler knelt down attempting to coax over, would allow handler to slowly approach and place clip leash while in kennel, able to exit kennel and remove leash via clip leash with no issues.
10/20/2026
Dog was being leashed to be moved into the indoor part of the kennel for daily cleanig procedures, once the leash was placed the dog began to thrash and leash bite. The dog redirected up towards the handlers hand making contact and not engaging further. Upon redirection the leash became loose around the dog's neck leading the dog to stick it's paw in the loop to loosen it further and escaping the leash and kennel. The dog ran from I building over to a gate next to F building where the handler eventually caught up to the dog and an EET staff member was able to leash the dog and guide them back to kennel without issue.
10/18/2026
Presented leash, dog would start to dodge leash placement.  Able to step into kennel & leash dog.  Would walked to PY with a stop & go style on leash while needing verbal coaxing.  Once in PY, dog would explore with a relaxed & wiggly body.  Approaching handler on own & when called over.  Would "SIT" for treats & take treats gently.  Would run & do zoomies then approach handler & jump up while leaning against handlers body for more petting, able to direct off without issues.  Picked up leash & verbally coaxed dog to walk into behavior taxi without issues for kennel return.  Rode well back to kennel.  Exited into kennel & allowed leash removal to be done by hand.
Interested parties should be counseled on providing this dog with proper decompression time in a new home.  Allowing time to adjust is important for their comfort and well-being.  Adopters should be counseled on proper dog-to-dog introductions, which should only occur after the dog has fully decompressed.
*This dog may need a behavior taxi to help with an easier kennel return*
10/17/2026
Closed outside for AM cleaning. Dog approached handler with soft body and wagging tail, took treats. Avoidant of leash placement, handler stepped into kennel, dog approached, able to slowly place leash, dog exited kennel then thrashed head briefly when feeling leash pressure, quickly settled and walked with light pull to yard, ignored kenneled dogs in passing. Affiliative with handler, front paws on lap soliciting attention, leaned into handler and allowed petting all over, panting, eyes soft, tongue lolled, explored yard but checked in with handler frequently soliciting more attention. Picked up leash and walked back to kennel, once in front of kennel dog stopped and began pulling away from handler, gave dog a moment to settle, dog stood with front paws against handler, panting, body soft, tail wagging, allowed handler to pick up and carry into kennel, able to reach in and remove leash by hand.
10/16/2026
During AM cleaning dog refused to move inside with verbal coaxing and treats, dog was laying agianst back kennel door and rerfused to move, went to back side and dog got up excited to exit kennel, would dodge attempts to leash, did a big loop and got leash on, opened kennel door and dog came out, allowed petting and walked polietly to other side of building, before entering building decided to use a back clip for easy return, dog remained calm with a soft body when attatching back clip leaning against handlers legs, entering the door way the dog walked forward and hit the end of the leash, the dog whipped backwards and vocalized, handler used leash pressure away to prevent from coming towards handler and dog began biting at leash, handler quickly opened the kennel door and allowed dog to move into kennel, dog would continue to bite at leash, once in kennel dog would vocalize at any slight pressure added so quickly removed leash with back clip, once leash was removed dog went and laid down in back of kennel. Offered treats once door was closed and dog came up and ate the ones tossed on the floor after a minute.
10/16/2026
Assisted with M&G. Adoptions staff had dog on leash on approach; dog had soft body language, wagging tail, leaned into handler's legs to seek attention. Some hesitation to walk on leash but easy to encourage forward with verbal coaxing. In yard, dog greeted customer with loose body language. Dog allowed all petting, sought attention. Handler took leash for return. Dog walked well, then stopped at open kennel gate. Dog began thrashing and crying out when any leash pressure was applied. Dog would twist body, jump up into air, then land on ground. Handler released all leash tension, spoke softly, was able to pet dog. Dog softened towards handler and adoptions staff. Ate wet food from hand but would not enter kennel for it. Dog continued to thrash, twist, and cry out when handler tried guiding dog into kennel. Second handler arrived, used sort board to guide dog forward. Dog fought against leash, began chewing it, whipped body around. Handler used straight arm on leash while closing gate. Dog continued to chew on leash. Handler spoke softly, dog dropped leash, came forward, panting but appearing to settle. Dog allowed slow leash removal by hand.
10/12/2026
Nervous, tense body, skin crawling, slow leash placement, tolerated some handling and vaccine booster with muzzle wrap restraint, thrashed slightly during restraint, slowly coaxed back into kennel with slight leash pressure, clip lead used to remove leash.
10/7/2026
Solicited attentions, Playful, Moderate to pull from kennel, Easy to return to kennel, Takes treats nicely, Easy/Loose Leash, Stop and go, Calm, Sit, Stepped into kennel to leash, some stopping when dogs were barking at him, appears potty trained, food motivated, affectionate, greets staff, friendly, good boy.
10/2/2026
Soft body, wagging tail, paws up on gate to solicit attention from handler. Placing YELLOW level based on kennel presence and intake notes.
*Dog should not be introduced to any other pets until end of 14-day decompression period. Potential adopters should be counseled on proper dog introductions, which must be slow and supervised. This approach is essential for the safety, comfort, and well-being of all pets involved.*
9/28/2026
dog was soft body, allowed petting/handling, walked on leash, allowed to carry into kennel with no issues
9/28/2026
walked on leash then stopped, carried, soft body, mild restraint for vaccines, allows all petting, allows all handling, carried to kennel

10/30/2026
Upon kennel approach, k9 came up to handler with soft body and happy tail wags. Handler was able to leash k9 with no issues. K9 bolted out of kennel and walked to clinic with hard pull. Once in clinic, k9 ran to multiple handlers and allowed all petting, played with toys and laid down. Slight pull back to kennel. K9 was hesitant to go back in kennel but allowed handler to pick up and "waddle" into kennel. Removed leash by hand with no issues and gave a couple more pets before closing kennel.
10/28/2026
Updating color due to NHO status.
10/27/2026
Pulled for AM cleaning. Very easy to leash, cooperative when walking, no pulling. He was very playful in the yard, very interested in toys. Did solicit attention. He was very easy to return to kennel.
10/27/2026
Bubba was easy to pull from his kennel. We spent time in the play yard, where he explored, played with a toy, and checked out the pool. We then took a short walk along the front of the shelter. He walked very good on a leash. Showed interest in other dogs but no barking or pulling. He was very difficult to return to his kennel. Three attempts were made to walk him back, but he was unwilling to enter. Additional staff assistance and a taxi were required to safely return him to his kennel.
10/27/2026
Dog was in main PY, responded to assistance needed in kennel return.  Handlers walked dog to side entrance of K-wing, all the way down the hall towards P3's, turned corner & entered into Life Room area without issues.  While approaching kennel room, dog would start to pull back on leash while panting heavy, resisting to enter.  Handler walked dog backwards to opposite side of double door entrance, would start to slowly jog with dog to go around the Life Room to approach door in opposite direction again, dog would do a sudden stop, started to pull back on leash again.  Handlers attempted to coax dog in by bouncing a ball, presenting a large stuffed toy & a rope toy, dog would not walk forward, started to pull back again each time while still panting heavy.  Allowed petting in between each toy & break.  Handlers attempted to lure with food dish, hot dogs & chicken, dog would not be treat motivated.  A behavior taxi was brought to dog, handler would hold leash taut while male handler would lift dog into behavior taxi.  While riding out of main building & to new kennel, dog would attempt to jump out of behavior taxi, able to use leash to keep dog into behavior taxi.  Exited into new kennel & allowed leash removal to be done by hand.
10/26/2026
Easy leashing, easy to remove and return from kennel. Strong pull on leash,  ignored the dogs while passing kennels and not bothered by reactive dogs and greeting people passing by. Found tug toy on yard and approached to play with soft wiggly body

10/28/26 12:18 This dog has started showing declining behaviors in shelter and demonstrated a recurring pattern of fluctuating in-kennel stress and anxiety, ranging from moderate to significant, over an extended period of time. These behaviors are often a response to the overwhelming sights, sounds, and confinement, along with the lack of choice or control over their environment. Although this dog continues to show appropriate behavior outside of the kennel with positive interactions with staff and volunteers, without intervention, well-being will continue to decline. Immediate placement is needed with an experienced adopter or New Hope Partner who can provide time and space to decompress in a calm, supportive home. Placement needed by close of business 11/2/26. May be at risk of euthanasia 11/3/26 or sooner if warranted.

sections.evaluation_comments:
10/27/2026
Dog was standing in back half of kennel, able to verbally coax forward to front half.  Leashed without issues.  Walked to small PY with a strong pull on leash, would stop to do intense sniffing.  Each time dog would notice a handler from afar, dog would stop walking & flag tail while low growling with a hard stare.  Once in small PY, dog would do an intense sniff of ground then start to pace along fence line, keeping tail flagged.  Would look up towards handler & start to do a fast tail wag while making a chuffing sound, dog a shake off of body & continue to pace.  Dog would keep turning & doing a hard stare towards handler while licking lips with a flagged tail then return to pacing along fence line.  Scattered treats onto ground, would not be interested in treats.  Handler would gently touch back of body, dog would stop pacing & flag tail while being still bodied looking up towards fence line then return to pacing.  Handler did not drop leash while in PY due to dog not settling.  Walked back to kennel with a strong pull on leash.  Opened building door, dog would pull back hard on leash while doing a low growl.  Handler called for assistance to have back half of kennel unlocked & gate wide open.  Dog would pull back on leash while walking to back half of kennel once gate was opened.  Both handlers would verbally coax dog past threshold while dog would keep stopping & pulling back on leash.  Assistant handler opened kennel divider & called dog inside from inside half of kennel, dog would enter.  Able to close kennel gate & removed leash with use of pre-attached clip leash.
10/26/2026
Laying at front of kennel with neutral body, stoic, gently accepted treat offered. Head shy with leash placement, retreated to back of kennel but able to coax back forward and place leash as handler knelt down. Exited with some pulling, flagged tail, moments of soft body on walk but became timid and froze in place when bumping into handler before entering yard, hunched over tense body, whale eye, able to coax thru into yard. Tolerant of pets on backside while placing leash stopper, explored around yard with flagged tail, intensely sniffing, some chuffing towards handler, would have some moments of wagging tail and soft body when called over by handler but wary of pets, flinched away from handler when extending hand out to pet head, dog would come forward to sniff treat offered but did not eat. After going potty dog had burst of overarousal/high energy, alarm barking at handler with flagged tail and some stiff body with slight play bow, handler would turn away from dog resulting in dog having zoomies before transitioning to loose tail wag and demand barking as handler picked up rope toy, would direct attention towards rope toy and played with toy until losing interest shortly after, would start to settle and approached handler as handler knelt down accepting pets with neutral soft wagging tail, able to pick up leash while petting. Strong pull back to kennel, flagged tail, resisted entering kennel by pulling hard away from kennel door, no interest in treats tossed in, ran into kennel when divider was opened, able to call dog forward to front of kennel and remove leash by hand.
10/25/2026
Soft bodied, tail wagging, took treats gently while solicitng attentions with handler. Needs full evaluation based on intake memo notes.
10/23/2026
Easy leashing, walking into Triage. Sat for treats. Tolerated restraint for vaccines and allowed all petting. Walked to kennel and entered with no issue

sections.evaluation_comments:
10/29/2026
Dog was at front of kennel, greeted handler with soft body, wagging tail curled above spine level, took treats through door, began jumping up as handler placed leash, exited quickly, pulling toward door, no approach to neighboring kennels but had piloerection and flagged tail. Strong pull, jumping up on handler with soft body once inside catchpen. Dog entered yard and urinated and defecated, followed handler with neutral body as they cleaned yard. Handler sat on bench, dog approached, soft wag, jumping up on their lap, pushing nose into their treat bag. Handler would take treat and lure into sit, dog was jumpy for treats but would eventually sit. Dog continued to push for treats, tolerated some petting but did not solicit, whining with touch, focused on treat bag, demand bark. Handler tossed treats to the side and grabbed a nearby stuffed toy, dog engaged in fetch with loose body, bringing toy back near handler, self entertaining, then dropping toy and trading for treat. Played fetch for a few minutes, dog remained loose and returned to handler each time, pushing toy against handlers legs while mouthing, would consistently drop for treat, handler continued to lure into "sit" position and dog was still jumpy/mouthy for treat but began to demonstrate sit faster with more repetitions. Handler pet dog, dog leaned into petting around neck, soft whining, handler pet towards rear and dog whipped head around, louder high pitch yowl, disengaged from handler. Handler played a bit more fetch then sat on bench, dog jumping up on their lap, handler would block them with hand on their chest, dog gave another high pitched vocalization, handler tossed treats aside and resumed playing fetch. Continued to attempt to pet between throws, dog allowed touch around neck, whining, did not solicit, and would continue to whip head around with touch on hind legs. Another dog walked past yard and this dog ran to fence, piloerection, stiff wag above spine level, weight forward, barking. Returned to handler for a moment but then returned to fence until dog out of sight. Continued to jump toward handler but could be redirected with treats and play. Handler opened catch pen door and dog followed them in, began to jump up and mouth at leash when handler picked it up, stopped as soon as handler dropped leash. Repeated behavior, able to pick up leash on third attempt with treat toss to distract. Strong pull back, alert, flagged tail, entered kennel, allowed leash removal by hand.
10/28/2026
Handler approached kennel front, dog greeted at gate with rounded posture, low tail and head hanging low. Handler reapproached from back kennel hoping to decrease any tension from neighboring dogs. Handler offered a few treats and began leashing attempts. Dog was highly avoidant and began pacing between front and back kennel. Handler lowered guillotine locking dog in back kennel. Handler was able to cast leash over head after several attempts and secure. Handler then walked dog out to nearest PY. Dog was tense in posture with tail flagged, dog pulled moderately. Once in PY handler adjusted leash stopper, attached leash extension and released dog. Dog kept to self for entire outing with continued tense posture and flagged tail. Dog sniffed around yard and marked. Dog approach empty kiddie pool and became fixated on sniffing it, dog would bump it and spook self.
